rows.citation: Gerkin RC, Jarvis RJ, Crook SM (2018). Towards systematic, data-driven validation of a collaborative, multi-scale model of Caenorhabditis elegans. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences, 373(1758), 20170381.
rows.model_type: OpenWorm multi-scale C. elegans models: NeuroML ion-channel (ChannelWorm), neuron and muscle-cell (c302), and whole-body locomotion (Sibernetic) models
rows.controlled_mutations: no - models change through ordinary development; no seeded single-fault mutants are described.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - tests span different experimental paradigms (IV curves, membrane-potential recordings, behaviour), but no designed stimulus battery per model is reported.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - tests score IV curves, interspike-interval distributions and action-potential waveforms against published data (e.g. Z-scores, sum-squared error).
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection or minimisation of test protocols is described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out models or train/test split; the authors state the testing shown is not exhaustive.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-assisted model edits are evaluated.
rows.software: SciUnit/NeuronUnit test suite: https://github.com/openworm/tests (GitHub API: exists, last push 2018-06-03); SciDash dashboard reported at http://dash.scidash.org (not checked)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Checks evolving models against experimental data, run continuously in CI. NeuroSem would compare each edited model against its own reference version, using refinement-calibrated tolerances, seeded mutants, and battery selection tested on held-out models. It reuses SciUnit-style testing rather than competing with it.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, authors, venue, volume/issue/article number, issued 2018-09-10); Europe PMC REST (PMID 30201844, PMC6158230, abstract); PMC full-text page via WebFetch (methods, repo URLs); GitHub REST API for openworm/tests.

rows.citation: Chintaluri C, Podlaski W, Bozelos PA, et al. (2025). An ion channel omnimodel for standardized biophysical neuron modelling. bioRxiv (preprint).
rows.model_type: Voltage-gated ion-channel kinetic models (NEURON channel models from the IonChannelGenealogy database), refit into one standard HH-style formulation; two pyramidal neuron models for spiking checks
rows.controlled_mutations: no - reformulation refits whole channel models; there are no recorded single-fault mutants or fault families.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - original and omnimodel channels are compared under several voltage-clamp protocols (activation, inactivation, deactivation, ramp, action-potential waveform).
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - agreement is measured as trace-level error (RMSE, area-based error, Frobenius norm) plus spiking comparisons in two neurons; no feature-extraction battery is reported.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - uses a fixed protocol set; no compact-battery selection is reported.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no train/test split of models or protocols is reported.
rows.ai_transformations: no - reformulation is done by automated least-squares fitting, not AI coding agents.
rows.software: ICG Explorer visualiser: https://icg-explorer.org/visualizer (HTTP 200 on 2026-09-13); an ICG GitHub repository is mentioned but its exact URL was not retrieved
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Tests one large, specific transformation (channel reformulation), mainly under voltage clamp and without an acceptance threshold. NeuroSem would target neuron-level current-clamp behaviour after arbitrary edits, adding calibrated tolerances, single-fault mutants, and greedy battery selection tested on held-out models and fault families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (posted-content, 7 authors, posted 2025-10-06); bioRxiv details API (v1, 2025-10-06, neuroscience, cc_by_nc, unpublished); Europe PMC REST (PPR1096349, abstract); bioRxiv v1.full-text page via WebFetch (methods summary, not verbatim); curl check of the ICG Explorer URL.

rows.citation: Smith LP, Malik-Sheriff RS, Nguyen TVN, et al. (2025). Verification and reproducible curation of the BioModels repository. PLOS Computational Biology, 21(12), e1013239.
rows.model_type: SBML ODE systems-biology models (curated BioModels entries) with SED-ML simulation-experiment descriptions
rows.controlled_mutations: no - the errors found in SED-ML files, models, wrappers and engines were pre-existing; no faults were deliberately seeded.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - each model gets a template SED-ML and, where curated, a full SED-ML experiment; there is no designed perturbation battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares raw numeric outputs across engines using numpy allclose (relative tolerance 1e-4, range-scaled absolute tolerance).
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of experiments or tests is described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - verification covers the whole repository; there is no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - curation used Python scripts and GitHub Actions; no AI agents are evaluated.
rows.software: https://github.com/sys-bio/temp-biomodels (GitHub API: exists, last push 2025-07-01); https://github.com/biosimulations/biosimulations-runutils (named in the paper, not API-checked)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Checks agreement across five engines for about a thousand systems-biology models under one fixed tolerance. NeuroSem would detect edit-induced behaviour change in neuron models using feature fingerprints, refinement-calibrated tolerances, seeded mutants, and held-out-evaluated battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (17 authors, PLOS Comput Biol 21(12) e1013239, issued 2025-12-04); Europe PMC REST (PMID 41343683, PMC12677764, abstract) and Europe PMC fullTextXML (methods: engines, tolerance rule, repos); GitHub REST API for sys-bio/temp-biomodels.

rows.citation: Dey S, Dimitrov A (2022). Mapping and Validating a Point Neuron Model on Intel's Neuromorphic Hardware Loihi. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 16, 883360.
rows.model_type: Leaky integrate-and-fire point neurons (GLIF parameters from the Allen Cell Types Database), BMTK reference simulation vs Loihi neuromorphic implementation
rows.controlled_mutations: no - validates one port to new hardware across 20 parameter sets; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - models are driven by a constant bias current and by frozen Poisson external spike inputs; there is no designed protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - agreement is measured on membrane-potential traces (RMSE, Pearson correlation); no electrophysiology feature set such as eFEL is reported.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no stimulus or test selection is described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - all parameter sets are used for validation; there is no held-out design.
rows.ai_transformations: no - the mapping to Loihi is done by hand-derived numerical transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Checks that one translation (classical simulator to neuromorphic chip) preserves LIF traces. NeuroSem would generalise to many edit types on conductance-based NeuroML models, using multi-protocol electrophysiology fingerprints with mutation-calibrated tolerances, optimized batteries and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (2 authors, Front Neuroinform 16, article 883360, issued 2022-05-30); Europe PMC REST (PMID 36726406, PMC9886005, abstract) and fullTextXML (stimuli, cost functions, repo); GitHub REST API for the data repo. The erratum DOI noted in found_via was not checked in this pass.

rows.citation: Olsen M, Raunak M (2019). Increasing Validity of Simulation Models Through Metamorphic Testing. IEEE Transactions on Reliability, 68(1), 91-108.
rows.model_type: General simulation models: agent-based (gossip propagation, cancer) and discrete-event (airport check-in and security)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - the abstract does not mention mutation analysis; the paywalled full text was not read.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - metamorphic relations vary model inputs/parameters and check the expected direction of behaviour change; these are not neuronal stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - the case studies are non-neuroscience simulations.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear - the abstract gives a framework and guidelines for applying metamorphic testing, with no reported optimization of which relations to test.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - three case studies are presented; no held-out evaluation is described in the abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-driven edits are evaluated.
rows.software: none reported in abstract (unclear; full text not accessed)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses metamorphic relations as pseudo-oracles to validate simulations against expected domain behaviour. NeuroSem would compare edited models against a reference neuron model using neuroscience stimuli, electrophysiology features, calibrated tolerances, seeded mutants, and held-out battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (IEEE Trans Reliab 68(1) 91-108, issued 2019-03; DOI registered with 2018 prefix); Semantic Scholar Graph API (abstract, DBLP key journals/tr/OlsenR19); Unpaywall API (no OA copy, lists year 2018). Full text not accessed.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org increasing validity of simulation models through metamorphic testing; WebSearch site:dblp.org metamorphic testing simulation models; Crossref (issued 2019; OpenAlex lists 2018)

rows.citation: Raunak MS, Olsen MM (2021). Metamorphic Testing on the Continuum of Verification and Validation of Simulation Models. 2021 IEEE/ACM 6th International Workshop on Metamorphic Testing (MET), 47-52.
rows.model_type: General modeling and simulation (M&S) models; conceptual workshop paper extending the authors' earlier metamorphic-testing-for-validation work
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - the abstract does not mention mutants; the full text was not accessed.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - metamorphic testing inherently compares related input executions; no stimulus battery is described.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear - the abstract describes reusing validation guidelines to elicit relations; no optimized selection is mentioned.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no empirical held-out evaluation is described in the abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-driven edits are evaluated.
rows.software: none reported in abstract (unclear; full text not accessed)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Frames metamorphic testing as serving both verification and validation of simulations. NeuroSem sits on the verification side (behaviour preservation after edits, not biological validity) and adds an empirical, mutation-calibrated, held-out-evaluated protocol battery for neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (proceedings-article, MET 2021, pp. 47-52, issued 2021-06); Semantic Scholar Graph API (abstract, DBLP key conf/icse-met/RaunakO21); Unpaywall API (no OA copy). Full text not accessed.
